creator: jploftofficial
title: Five UX features a 10-year app agency puts in almost every app: skeleton loaders, autofill, optimistic UI, save state, proper error handling
claims: Creator has built apps for over 10 years
Skeleton loaders make an app 'feel 100 times faster and more polished' vs a spinner
Autofill/prefill removes 'a ridiculous amount of friction'
Optimistic UI: update immediately, process in background, reverse only on failure
Save state: drafts, unfinished forms, filters, searches, carts should survive app close
Error handling: catch errors, preserve progress, explain in plain language, give a retry button; never show a raw 404/backend message or wipe user work
how_to_steps: Replace loading spinners with skeleton loaders that mirror the content layout
Use native autofill and prefill any field the app already knows (name, email, phone)
Apply optimistic UI to save/like/delete/complete actions; roll back on server error
Persist drafts, form progress, filters, searches and carts; restore on return
Wrap API/network failures: preserve state, show human-readable message, offer 'try again'
on_screen_only: Title card: 'Here are 5 features I'd put in almost EVERY app (after building apps for 10+ years)'

relevance.why: Directly applicable product-quality checklist for anyone shipping apps with Claude Code; these are the polish items vibe-coded apps most often lack.

implement_score.why: Zero cost: paste these five rules into CLAUDE.md / a UI-standards skill so every new screen gets skeletons, prefill, optimistic updates, draft persistence and friendly error states by default.

verify: None of this is tool-specific; just confirm the patterns fit the stack (e.g. optimistic UI with your data layer)
